examples.scenario: Publicly exposed AWS S3 bucket containing sensitive PII data due to overly permissive bucket policy allowing anonymous user GetObject access.

technical_data.http_request:
GET /customer-data-bucket/pii/20240415_customer_list.csv HTTP/1.1
Host: customer-data-bucket.s3.amazonaws.com
User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
Accept: */*

indicators: S3 bucket policy allowing "Principal": "*" with s3:GetObject
CloudTrail entries showing Anonymous user identity accessing sensitive keys
HTTP GET requests from unusual external IPs to S3 objects under /pii/
Presence of CSV or JSON files with PII fields in bucket
examples.detection_method: Implement continuous bucket policy scanning using AWS Config rules or third-party CSPM tools to detect public read permissions; monitor CloudTrail logs for GetObject events with Anonymous user identities; alert on downloads of sensitive prefixes (e.g., /pii/); use data loss prevention (DLP) for content inspection of data accessed.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
T1552.001 - Credentials in Files: Cloud Storage Object

indicators: GCS bucket IAM policy with "allUsers" member assigned roles/storage.objectViewer
Access logs showing anonymous IPs downloading confidential PDF and XLSX files
Publicly accessible bucket listing via API
Presence of sensitive document metadata and filenames in bucket
examples.detection_method: Use GCP Security Command Center or custom scripts to audit bucket IAM policies for allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers bindings; monitor access logs for unauthenticated object retrievals; automate alerts on sensitive filename patterns and large downloads from public buckets.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

examples.scenario: Azure Blob Storage container set to 'Container (anonymous read access for containers and blobs)' allowing external actors to download internal backup archives containing database dumps.

technical_data.azure_cli_get_access_level: az storage container show --account-name corpstorageacct --name db-backups --query 'publicAccess'
technical_data.suspect_backup_file_preview:
MSSQL Database Backup Header:
Database Name: ProdDB
Backup Type: Full
Backup Start Date: 2024-06-01 00:00:00
Backup Finish Date: 2024-06-01 01:15:30

indicators: Azure Blob container public access level set to 'container' or 'blob'
Storage analytics logs showing anonymous GetBlob operations from external IPs
Presence of large .bak files (database backups) downloadable without authentication
Command-line downloads using wget or curl from blob URLs
examples.detection_method: Configure Azure Policy to disallow public read access to sensitive storage containers; enable and review Storage Analytics Logging for anonymous access patterns; use Azure Defender for Storage to detect unusual access; alert on downloads of backup file extensions from publicly accessible containers.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
T1537 - Transfer Data to Cloud Account
T1110 - Brute Force (if used to escalate access)
